title: No way to silence the `litmodels` advertisement
body:
### Bug description

Running `trainer.fit` with default checkpointing currently prints
```
💡 Tip: For seamless cloud uploads and versioning, try installing [litmodels](https://pypi.org/project/litmodels/) to enable LitModelCheckpoint, which syncs automatically with the Lightning model registry.
``` 

This advertisement is displayed even if `litmodels` is installed, but not used.

I don't need any "cloud uploads and versioning". In fact, I am often working with proprietary models and restricted data. I sincerely hope that this "tip" isn't suggesting that `lightning` is going to automatically upload anything anywhere (whether I have this `litmodels` package installed or not).

Please, do one of the following (in order of personal preference):
1) remove this advertisement
2) only show this advertisement when appropriate (perhaps, if you detect that the user does have `litmodels` installed or is already using some "cloud"-related stuff)
3) provide a way to silence this advertisement

### What version are you seeing the problem on?

v2.5

### Reproduced in studio

_No response_

### How to reproduce the bug

```python
model = ...
dl_train = ...
dl_valid = ...
trainer = L.Trainer(accelerator="auto", max_epochs=3)
trainer.fit(model, dl_train, dl_valid)


As far as I can tell, the model and dataloaders are irrelevant to this issue.
```

### Error messages and logs

```
💡 Tip: For seamless cloud uploads and versioning, try installing [litmodels](https://pypi.org/project/litmodels/) to enable LitModelCheckpoint, which syncs automatically with the Lightning model registry.
```


### Environment

<details>
  <summary>Current environment</summary>

```
#- PyTorch Lightning Version (e.g., 2.5.0): 2.5.5
#- PyTorch Version (e.g., 2.5): 2.8.0
#- Python version (e.g., 3.12): 3.12.11
#- OS (e.g., Linux): Linux
#- CUDA/cuDNN version: 12.8
#- GPU models and configuration: any model, default configuration
#- How you installed Lightning(`conda`, `pip`, source): pip
```

</details>


### More info

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
reporter
comments.body:
By "silence this advertisement" I meant by configuring the `Trainer`. For example, if the user is explicitly requesting `enable_checkpointing=True` or passing a checkpoint callback, then they are probably not interested in your cloud-based checkpointing alternative.

Obviously, any warning or message can be filtered out in a bunch of ways (we are working in a Turing-complete language, after all). But I don't think that it's appropriate to expect that the user will add custom log filtering in order to remove ads from the output of the program.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi @reporter,

`litmodels` is a new product from the [Lightning team](https://lightning.ai/), and this tip helps users discover and try it so we can gather early feedback.

We understand some users may not want such messages, especially in controlled environments. You’re right, users shouldn’t need to modify logging just to hide non-essential tips. We’ll revisit how and when these are shown and likely add a Trainer flag or env variable to disable them.

> **The goal isn’t to advertise but to surface new integrations in a lightweight way, while keeping the experience clean and predictable**.

Thanks for the thoughtful feedback!

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
> Hi [@reporter](https://github.com/reporter), This might be intentional to help promote the package, but in case anyone prefers to filter the tip message, the following snippet seemed to work for me:
> 
> import logging
> 
> class TipFilter(logging.Filter):
>     def filter(self, record):
>         return "💡 Tip" not in record.getMessage()
> 
> logging.getLogger('lightning.pytorch.utilities.rank_zero').addFilter(TipFilter())

I'm wondering if it makes sense to introduce a dedicated tips logger for this kind of use case? So that 1st, allow the Lightning team to surface tips or best practices in a more structured way, and 2nd, give users explicit control over whether they want to see these tips.

for instance, we could have a dedicated logger namespace:
```python
tip_logger = logging.getLogger("lightning.tips")


# in both callback connector and logger connector where the tips are raised.
tip_logger.info("The original tips")

# in users code space
tip_logger.disable = True
```

This way, users can easily opt out of tips by disabling the logger, while still leave all other important information intact.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: While you're designing your custom logging solution, could you please revert this change? There is enough warning spam in the world without deliberate ads in log output. It's even worse when running with DDP, when this "helpful tip" is printed for every single process. I did not find that the suggested log filtering works.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi @participant5, sorry for the inconvenience. We're discussing on dropping it.

Although, it shouldn't have printed it for every single process, as we use `rank_zero_info`.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi @participant6 @reporter @participant5 ,

We added a flag to turn this off:

```python
Trainer(
        ...,
        suggest_integrations=False, # default True
    )
```

Thanks for your patience.
